test_command: dotnet build api/Biolog.Api/Biolog.Api.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.IntegrationTests/Biolog.IntegrationTests.csproj && dotnet test tests/dotnet/Biolog.UnitTests/Biolog.UnitTests.csproj && bash scripts/check-module-project-references.sh && python3 scripts/check-contract-freeze.py && bash scripts/secret-scan.sh && (cd web && npx tsc --noEmit)
notes:
Round 2 of the post-acceptance BIO-OPS-002 remediation. Round 1 (commits 56927c7/0a43844) fixed the two named findings in shape but not in the supported/default configuration - Seyi's round-2 review (evidence b2e9369) found both still didn't close.

SY-OPS002-03 (High): round 1's DemoSessionTenantResolver had 'beta' silently fall back to the SAME tenant as alpha when WebSessionBridge:SyntheticTenantIdBeta was unconfigured. Seyi correctly identified this as the IDENTICAL cosmetic-switch defect OPS002-F01 was originally about, moved one level down - in the default/supported config (nobody sets the beta key today), selecting beta still silently resolved to alpha's tenant, and round 1's own new test (OPS002_F01_beta_falls_back_to_the_same_tenant_as_alpha_when_the_second_key_is_unconfigured) had literally encoded that fallback as the intended behavior rather than testing against it. Fixed: ResolveSyntheticTenantId now returns null (not a fallback) when the claimed tenant's own config key is unset, and TryVerify rejects the whole token in that case - falls through to ordinary host-channel resolution, never a substituted tenant. This mirrors this exact class's own already-established 'optional config gap' precedent for a missing/too-short secret (LoadFromConfiguration: unconfigured means the mechanism never activates), applied one level down to a missing per-tenant mapping instead of a missing secret. Rewrote the round-1 HTTP test to assert rejection (401 demo_session_invalid) instead of fallback, and rewrote+added a matching pair of unit tests directly against TenantContextMiddleware (beta resolves to ITS OWN tenant when configured; beta falls through to host resolution, not alpha's tenant, when unconfigured) - the second of these replaces a PRE-EXISTING TD-WEB-PROVENANCE-BRIDGE round-5 test that asserted the original round-1 cosmetic bug as intended behavior ('the claimed tenantId has no effect on which tenant is resolved'), which my OWN fix now correctly breaks and had to update.

SY-OPS002-04 (High): round 1's startDemoSession set the session cookie THEN called the audit endpoint fire-and-forget (not awaited), swallowing any failure - a successful switch (cookie committed) could leave zero audit trail if the write failed, the opposite of what AC04 needs. Seyi required the same audit-before-commit discipline already established on this floor (BIO-DEV-004's remote jobs: audited through the real shared sink BEFORE the action, never best-effort after). Fixed: recordContextChangeAudit is now called and AWAITED BEFORE jar.set(...), returns a boolean success flag instead of void, and startDemoSession clears the cookie and returns early on failure - exactly the same fail-closed shape that function already uses for every other failure mode (bad tenant/role id, issuance disabled, token too short). Disclosed, accepted consequence (documented in both functions' own headers and in docs/features/bio-ten-002/README.md): a web deployment with no reachable Biolog.Api backend can no longer establish a demo session cookie at all. Confirmed this is not a practical regression: no SIMULATION-mode test (the default everywhere) reads this HttpOnly cookie, and the only three specs that do (BIOLOG_TDWEBPROV_LIVE_TESTS/BIOLOG_TEN003_LIVE_TESTS/BIOLOG_ATT003_LIVE_TESTS) already require a real reachable backend to run at all - grepped for every reference to SESSION_TOKEN_COOKIE/startDemoSession across tests/frontend before concluding this.

Verification: dotnet build clean (0 warnings/errors). Biolog.UnitTests 211/211 (was 210, +1 net - one test rewritten, one new one added). Full Biolog.IntegrationTests 288/288 (same count as round 1 - the round-1 HTTP test was rewritten in place, not added to, zero regression elsewhere). module-reference/contract-freeze/secret-scan all PASS. web tsc --noEmit clean. No Playwright re-run - same reasoning as round 1's own evidence: the only web diff is a server-side effect behind an already-approved control, with no new UI surface, and the live specs that DO exercise this cookie already require a backend precondition my change doesn't change.

Orchestration: still DONE status, late-commit/builder-complete both refuse as in round 1 - committed directly on feature/BIO-TEN-002 again, tracked via this new round-2 evidence file (mirroring this story's own now-established per-round-file convention from round 1).
